provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Food family batch, event archetype. Order-form-first: most custom cake bakers run on DMs. Many are home bakers, so prices stay small and pickup details avoid home addresses. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Occasion, pickup date, servings needed, tiers, flavour and filling, a slot for the customer's inspiration pictures, budget range, and pickup or delivery, with servings and date asked first
pageStructurePlus.why: Custom cake DMs go back and forth for days. A form that asks the date and servings first turns a week of messages into one reply with a price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Round and sheet cake sizes in inches with how many servings each feeds, tier combinations, the starting price per serving the baker sets, and what adds cost: sugar flowers, fondant, sculpted or tall cakes
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers don't know how many people a six-inch cake feeds. They decide on servings and a starting price before they ever look at design.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cake flavours, fillings and buttercream or ganache options, seasonal flavours, and which ones the baker can make eggless or dairy-free, in the baker's own words
pageStructurePlus.why: Flavour is the second question after price, and party hosts need to know early whether the cake works for a guest who avoids eggs or dairy.

pageStructurePlus.section: Lead times, pickup and cake delivery
pageStructurePlus.contains: How far ahead to order custom cakes, cupcakes and cookies, the rush order policy, pickup windows and instructions, tiered cake delivery and setup, and how to carry a cake home
pageStructurePlus.why: Last-minute buyers need to know right away whether the bakery can do Saturday. A clear lead-time table saves the baker a dozen no-thank-you replies.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Today's breads, pastries and cookies in the case, weekend bread pre-orders, and the usual sell-out time for favourites like croissants or sourdough loaves
pageStructurePlus.why: Walk-in bakery customers want to know what's in the case before they drive over, and a sold-out shelf is the most common disappointment.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A pickup tasting box of several cake flavours and fillings for couples, its fee, the pickup days, and how the fee comes off the wedding cake order
pageStructurePlus.why: Couples choose a wedding cake baker after tasting. A tasting box they can pick up beats trying to schedule a sit-down appointment.

designDirections.name: Order a Cake
designDirections.bestFor: Home and storefront bakers whose orders are birthday cakes, cupcakes and cookie sets
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom birthday cakes and cupcakes in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach and soft rounded type feel like a party box, and the stacked cards put the cake order form and servings guide first.

designDirections.name: Bakery Window
designDirections.bestFor: Bakeries with a counter and a custom cake side, showing cakes by occasion beside the daily case
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom cakes and fresh bread, baked daily in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Olive Grove. The cream ground flatters crust and buttercream, and the bookish serif reads like a hand-lettered bakery sign.

designDirections.name: Wedding Cake Atelier
designDirections.bestFor: Wedding cake designers with sugar flowers and tall tiers who book by consultation
designDirections.headlineSample: Wedding cakes, designed and baked in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Gallery white with a Didone display lets one tall wedding cake fill the screen like a gallery piece, and signals a bespoke price without saying it.

openers.line: Your bakery's Google listing has lovely reviews and no website, so someone searching for a custom birthday cake can't see your cakes or a starting price before they pick.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your bio says to DM for custom cake orders. That's a lot of back and forth about servings and dates that one order form could ask in a single go.
openers.hook: Check the bio for 'DM to order' or 'message for quotes'. Note the exact wording.
openers.linkLine: A custom cake order form that asks the right questions: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a starting price for a custom cake anywhere on your pages. A parent with a budget usually orders from the baker who says what a tiered cake starts at.
openers.hook: Check highlights, pinned posts and the listing for any cake prices. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Cake servings and starting prices on one page: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Order form broken on a phone
openers.line: The cake order link in your bio opens a form that's hard to fill in on a phone and never asks for the pickup date. Most cake orders start on a phone at night.
openers.hook: Only if they have a form. Open it on your phone and try it. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same cake order form, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples book wedding cake tastings in the winter for spring and summer. A bakery with tasting boxes and a wedding gallery gets those dates first.
openers.hook: Use this from November to March. Look for any wedding cake posts from last season.
openers.linkLine: Wedding cakes and tasting boxes, ready to order: {demo-link}

openers.line: Thanksgiving pies and Christmas cookie boxes are coming, and right now holiday bakery orders come in by DM and get tracked on paper.
openers.hook: Use this from October to early December. Check for last year's pie or cookie box posts.
openers.linkLine: A holiday bakery pre-order page with pickup slots: {demo-link}

openers.line: Graduation party season means sheet cakes and cupcake towers for every weekend in May and June. A cake page with servings and a date check catches those orders early.
openers.hook: Use this from March to May. Look for graduation cake posts from last year.

openers.line: You posted that your cake calendar is full for the next few weekends. A booking calendar that shows open dates saves you answering every request with a no.
openers.hook: Look for 'booked up', 'no more orders this month' or 'closed for orders' posts. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A cake calendar that shows open dates: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the bakery is hiring a cake decorator. Good decorators look at whether the bakery seems busy and organised before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story or a help-wanted sign. Note the role and the date.
openers.linkLine: A bakery page with a join-the-team section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts show tiered cakes set up at venues all over the area. A delivery page with towns, fees and setup times stops couples assuming you won't drive a wedding cake that far.
openers.hook: List the venues or towns in their wedding cake posts. Note the farthest one.
openers.linkLine: Your cake delivery area and setup on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the cake tasted even better than it looked. That belongs right next to the cake order form, not buried on Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a specific cake or flavour. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your cake reviews next to the order form: {demo-link}

openers.line: You bake from home, and pickup details end up in DMs one customer at a time. A cake page with pickup windows and instructions, without your home address public, handles it.
openers.hook: Only if they say 'home bakery' or 'cottage bakery'. Never claim or question any licence; just note the pickup set-up.
openers.linkLine: A home bakery page with pickup windows: {demo-link}

openers.line: People keep asking in your comments what cake flavours you do and whether there's an eggless option. A flavours and fillings page answers that before they order elsewhere.
openers.hook: Find comments asking about flavours, gluten, eggs or dairy. Never state a dietary fact; the baker sets every word.
openers.linkLine: A cake flavours and fillings page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your cake orders come from friends of friends and school parents. When that circle is booked out, the next customer looks for a bakery online.
openers.hook: Look for reviews or comments like 'made my daughter's cake' or 'recommended by a friend'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Where a new cake customer would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is gorgeous cake work. It should be the first thing a new customer sees on a bakery page, not lost in the grid.
openers.hook: Pick their newest cake post and name it exactly: the occasion, tiers and the standout detail.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is beautiful cake work.

I looked for a way to order a custom cake from {Business Name} without a long DM thread and couldn't find one. I put together a sample bakery page with a cake order form that asks the date and servings first, a servings guide and a flavours page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case this got lost under the order requests. Here's the sample bakery page for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a custom cake order form, servings and starting prices you set, a flavours page and pickup instructions. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for bakeries and custom cake makers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries, I know your messages are mostly cake orders. Short version: I built a sample page for {Business Name} with a cake order form that asks date and servings first, a servings guide and a flavours page, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and menu changes. For a bakery like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"A few custom cake orders cover it, and the form saves you evenings of DMs. Could I walk you through it for ten minutes on a day you're not decorating?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and the order form goes live first."

objections.objection: All my cake orders come through Instagram.
objections.handler: "Keep posting there. The order form just replaces the back and forth: the date, servings and flavour arrive in one message, and the DM becomes a link."

objections.objection: Every cake is custom, I can't list prices.
objections.handler: "You don't list a final price. A starting price per serving and what adds cost lets people self-sort, and you still quote each cake."

objections.objection: I'm a home baker, I'm not a real bakery.
objections.handler: "Home bakers are exactly who this is for. The page shows pickup windows and instructions without putting your address online, and it makes a one-oven business look intentional."

objections.objection: I'm already booked out most weekends.
objections.handler: "Then the site is for choosing better orders. Clear starting prices and lead times filter the last-minute, low-budget requests before they reach you."

objections.objection: My cousin made me a free site.
objections.handler: "Keep it if it takes orders well. If it doesn't ask for the date and servings, you're still doing the work in DMs. That form is the part I'd add."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's an order form, a servings guide and a cake gallery. A few custom orders cover it."

email.subject: Cake order page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for bakeries in {City}, and I put together a sample cake order page for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link so you can look when the oven's off. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} cake page demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — holiday pie and cookie box orders start landing in a few weeks, and wedding cake couples begin booking tastings in January. Thought of you.

The sample bakery page is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a handful of custom cake orders. Many cake makers work from home and every dollar is weighed against ingredients.
Price the cake gallery by occasion count, not page count: birthdays, weddings, baby showers and cupcakes each need their own set.
The order form is the line that sells the site. Price it on its questions and logic, not as a contact page.
Charge storefront bakeries for the daily case and bread pre-orders; home bakers usually don't need them.
Holiday pre-order pages sell in October and wedding tasting boxes in November, never during the rush.
Keep monthly add-ons under the profit on one birthday cake, or they'll be cancelled in a slow January.

lineItems.item: Custom cake order form with logic
lineItems.description: Max with servings-based size suggestions, lead-time blocking for rush dates, inspiration picture upload and a deposit step.
Max when each occasion has its own starting price, flavour notes and an order button prefilled for that cake type.
Max with round, sheet and tiered sizes, a servings chart and a clear list of what adds cost.

lineItems.item: Holiday pre-order page with pickup slots
lineItems.description: Max with pickup slot limits per hour, a cut-off date and a printable bake list for each day.

lineItems.item: Daily case and bread pre-order board
lineItems.description: Max when the case updates from a phone, items show sold out, and weekend loaves can be reserved.
Max with flavour choice, pickup days, fee payment and the fee credited on the wedding cake order.
Max when the order form, flavours and pickup instructions are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Cake photo backdrop and lighting setup
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A simple backdrop and light set up in the bakery, plus one session shooting your best cakes, so every finished cake gets a clean photo before pickup."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, before the next busy weekend of custom orders.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the bakery
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "New cake and pastry photos on your Google profile every week, with the occasion named, so people searching for a custom cake nearby see fresh work."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after cake pickup
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day after the party, the customer gets a short text asking how the cake went down, while the photos are still in their camera roll."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30. The easiest second sale for a bakery.

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday pies and cookie box campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A November push for holiday pies and cookie boxes, on the bakery page and in your stories, with a cut-off date so the oven schedule stays sane."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run from early November to mid-December.

whatElseYouSell.name: Engagement season wedding cake push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A January campaign to newly engaged couples pointing at the wedding cake gallery and tasting boxes, before the spring calendar fills."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, run from late December to February.

whatElseYouSell.name: Cake box sticker and order card artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A sticker for every cake box and a small card with the order code, so every party guest who loved the cake knows where to order the next one."

whatElseYouSell.name: Graduation and party season push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A spring push for graduation sheet cakes and cupcake towers, sized by servings, so May weekends fill before the requests turn frantic."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run from March to May.

withoutAI.route: The coffee shop that stocks their pastries
withoutAI.whoPays: The café owner, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The café that sells your croissants has no menu online. They'd trust the bakery that fills their pastry case."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Wholesale accounts see the bakery's site and want the same. The baker's word gets you the meeting.

withoutAI.route: The cake supply shop they buy from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The cake supply shop where you buy boxes and fondant sells to every baker in town and runs decorating classes with a paper sign-up. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply shops have a store, classes and a customer list of bakers. A regular customer is the warmest introduction.

withoutAI.route: The wedding venues where their cakes are set up
withoutAI.whoPays: The venue, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The venue where your wedding cakes are set up every month has no page listing its dessert vendors. The bakery can be the first name on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Venues trust vendors who show up on time with a perfect cake. That trust is your introduction.

withoutAI.whoPays: Each decorator, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The balloon decorator who works the same birthday parties as your cakes takes every booking by DM too. Same problem, same fix."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Party vendors refer each other constantly. A cake maker sits in the middle of the kids' party circle.

withoutAI.route: Florists who supply fresh cake flowers
withoutAI.whoPays: The florist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The florist who supplies flowers for your wedding cakes needs a wedding enquiry page too. The baker can make the introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Florists and cake designers share couples. The second build in a wedding circle is the easiest.

withoutAI.route: The kids' party venue next door
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The play centre that hosts birthday parties sends families to your bakery for cakes. Their party booking page should sell a cake add-on."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Party venues want a bigger booking per family. A cake add-on page benefits both the venue and the bakery.

withAI.route: Wholesale pastry reorder assistant for the café
withAI.pitchLine: "The café texts tomorrow's pastry order at close, and the bakery gets a clean bake list by account before the ovens go on."
withAI.whyItWorks: Wholesale orders by text get missed. The bakery client knows exactly how its cafés order.

withAI.route: Decorating class booking assistant for the supply shop
withAI.pitchLine: "People ask about cake decorating classes at any hour and get dates, skill level and a booking link from the shop's own class list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Classes fill or fail on quick answers. The supply shop knows the baker client and trusts the introduction.

withAI.route: Dessert vendor matcher for the venue
withAI.pitchLine: "Couples describe their wedding cake style and guest count, and the venue's assistant suggests bakers from its approved list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venues answer dessert vendor questions on every tour. The cake baker is the first name on the list.

withAI.route: Balloon and party quote assistant for decorators
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents describe the party theme and size and get a first balloon quote range and a cake suggestion from the partner bakery."
withAI.whyItWorks: Decorators answer how-much DMs all day. Pairing quotes with the bakery client makes both businesses bigger.

withAI.route: Wedding flower enquiry assistant for the florist
withAI.pitchLine: "Couples share their colours and date and get the florist's starting packages and a consultation link, cake flowers included."
withAI.whyItWorks: Florists juggle enquiries during their busiest weeks. The cake designer client already shares couples with them.

withAI.route: Party add-on assistant for the kids' party venue
withAI.pitchLine: "Families booking a party get offered a birthday cake from the partner bakery, sized to their guest count, with the order passed straight to the baker."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venues earn more per booking and the bakery gets orders. Both sides pay because both sides win.

softwareAI.name: Instant reply to custom cake requests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every cake request gets an instant reply with lead times, the servings guide and when you'll quote, so nobody orders from another bakery while waiting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build or day 14. Needs their lead times and the reply wording the baker approves.

softwareAI.name: Cake deposit at order
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A custom cake is only on the calendar once the deposit is paid, so a no-show order no longer leaves you holding a finished three-tier cake."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 14, or the first time they mention an unpaid cake. Needs their deposit rule and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Bake calendar with daily order limits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Set how many cakes you can make each day, and the order form closes a date when it's full, so you stop saying yes to a fourth wedding cake on one Saturday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their weekly capacity and days off.

softwareAI.name: Cake DM answers for flavours, prices and dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'How much for a two-tier cake for thirty' and 'are you free Saturday' get answered from your servings guide and calendar, with the order form link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the servings guide, flavours and calendar kept current. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Pickup reminders with instructions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day before, every cake customer gets a pickup time, where to park and how to carry the cake flat, so pickups run on time and cakes arrive whole."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their pickup windows and instructions.

softwareAI.name: Weekend bread and pastry pre-orders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Regulars reserve Saturday sourdough and croissants by Thursday, so the bakery bakes to real orders and the favourites stop selling out by nine."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for storefront bakeries. Needs the weekend menu and a pre-order cut-off.

softwareAI.name: Inspiration picture reader for cake quotes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A customer uploads the cake they saw online, and you get a note on tiers, techniques and the likely price band from your own rules before you reply."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the baker's pricing rules for decoration types. The baker always sets the final quote. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Servings and price calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers enter their guest count and get the cake sizes that fit and a starting price from your own chart, before they fill in the order form."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their size chart and per-serving starting prices.

softwareAI.name: Cake post caption writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post the finished cake and get a caption in your voice with the occasion, flavour and an order link, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a handful of past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Birthday reorder reminder a year later
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Six weeks before last year's birthday cake date, the parent gets a friendly note asking if they want this year's cake from the same bakery."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once there is order history with occasions and dates.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the bakery
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every bakery review gets a warm reply drafted in your voice that mentions the cake or pastry they loved, ready to approve while the oven runs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Daily bake list from orders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each morning the bakery gets one list: which cakes, layers, fillings and frostings to make today for this week's pickups."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the order form live and their recipes named.

softwareAI.name: Holiday order cut-off countdown
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The pie and cookie box page counts down to the order cut-off and closes on time, so the bakery isn't taking Thanksgiving orders on Wednesday night."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: October. Needs the holiday menu, the cut-off date and the pickup slots.

softwareAI.name: Bakery phone answering for cake orders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "With your hands in buttercream, calls about cake orders still get answered, the date and servings captured and the order form texted over."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for storefront bakeries. Needs the servings guide, calendar and policies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Ingredient cost per cake
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each cake size really costs in butter, flour and fondant, so your per-serving price keeps up when ingredient prices jump."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs recipes with quantities and current supplier prices.

softwareAI.name: Cake flavour matcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers answer a few questions about the party and the guest of honour, and get two or three cake and filling pairings from your own flavour list."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the flavours and fillings list with the baker's pairing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Wholesale ordering portal for cafés
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Cafés that stock your pastries order tomorrow's bakery delivery from a simple portal with their own prices and a cut-off time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for bakeries with wholesale accounts. Needs the wholesale price list and delivery days.

softwareAI.name: Dietary questions from the baker's own notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers ask whether a cake can be eggless or nut-free and get only the baker's approved answer, or a message that the baker will reply personally."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs written notes from the baker, approved and re-approved at every flavour change. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cookie and cupcake set builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers build a box of decorated cookies or cupcakes by quantity, colour and theme, pay, and pick a pickup slot from the bakery calendar."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their set sizes, themes and prices.

softwareAI.name: Bakery case demand forecaster
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each evening it suggests tomorrow's bake for the case from past sales by weekday, weather and pre-orders, so fewer loaves go stale and fewer favourites sell out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, for storefront bakeries with sales history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the cake order form for home bakers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every home cake maker runs orders through DMs. A servings-first cake order form with a deposit and calendar is a cheap monthly product."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: There are many home bakers, each with a tiny budget. A low monthly price at volume beats custom builds.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home baker and cottage food associations
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every member baker a cake order page and the association a directory where parents can find a local cake maker."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want member benefits that matter. An order page is the thing every member asks about.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your customers are cake makers who need order pages. Offer the template as a perk with every account, and they'll keep buying supplies from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Supply distributors compete on loyalty. A tool their bakers use daily is stickier than a discount.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Baking and pastry school graduate launch kits
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Graduates who start a cake business leave with an order page and a servings guide. It's a reason to enrol in your program."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools sell outcomes. Each graduating class brings a fresh group of new bakery owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your in-store bakery takes custom cake orders on paper slips. An online cake order form with pickup slots fills the counter's calendar."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Independent grocers run several stores and want to compete with chains online. One frame rolls out per store.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every location books birthday parties and sends families out for cakes. A cake add-on in your party booking makes each booking bigger."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains want more revenue per party. The bakery client proves the add-on works at one location.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Café and coffee chains buying wholesale pastry
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your cafés order pastries from several bakeries by text. One ordering portal for all your bakery suppliers saves your managers time."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Café groups buy from many local bakers. The bakery client already sells to one of them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your cake boxes go to bakers all over the country. A free order-page template with your boxes in the photos is a marketing program, not a cost."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Packaging makers need reasons for bakers to pick their brand. A useful tool beats another catalogue.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Wedding expo organisers' dessert vendor pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Engaged couples walk the expo floor tasting cake samples. Let each dessert baker take tasting box orders right there from a page with their flavours."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Organisers sell booths on results. Tasting boxes ordered at the show are a result they can sell.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label cake order template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency turns away bakers because the budget is small. License my servings-first cake order template and say yes at a profit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies get bakery enquiries they can't price. A ready template lets them sell and pay you per site.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Shoppers want to reserve bread and pastries from market bakers before Saturday. A pre-order page for every bakery vendor sells out the stalls."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Markets want vendors to do well so they return. A shared pre-order page is a market-wide benefit.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One cake maker per suburb, then the next
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New bakery clients in new suburbs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one custom cake maker per suburb around {City}. Parents order cakes close to home, so the next suburb is a fresh market."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Cake customers rarely drive far for a birthday cake. Splitting by suburb keeps every client happy and the template reusable.

upsellLadder.offer: Bakery site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The bakery site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new flavour or a price change is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a cake that was never picked up or paid for.
